title: Make it survive a node kill
intro: Don't pick the fault-tolerant architecture — build it.
briefing: The inspector will kill any ONE middle component of your system. Wire a topology where a client can still reach data afterwards. Clients must enter through the load balancer — never straight to an app server.

rules.label: Clients enter through the load balancer
No client talks to an app server directly
No client touches the database directly
Inspector's test: kill any one middle node — a client still reaches data

debrief:
The spec is spatial redundancy end to end — and the part most people miss is the FRONT DOOR: with one load balancer, killing it cuts every client off, so the inspection forces a second LB just as much as the second app replica. 'No single point of failure' means every middle node is bypassable: at least two LBs, two apps, and a database replica, wired so an alternative path always exists. In production you'd go further and CROSS-connect (each LB to every app, each app to every DB node) — not for the single-kill test you just passed, but so one failure doesn't halve your capacity and two failures don't strand a whole chain. Redundancy is a property of paths, not a count of boxes.
